requirement: Serve MCP resources by URI, including FastMCP-like templates such as users://{user_id}/profile, without letting parameters match more than one path segment.
skeleton: A ResourceError, a ResourceTemplate compiling escaped literals and slash-free named groups with fullmatch and unquote, and a ResourceRegistry preferring exact URIs.
caption: FastMCP-style resources and URI templates written in the standard library with re, urllib.parse unquote and collections.abc and no third-party imports. ResourceError covers malformed templates and unmatched URIs. ResourceTemplate splits the template on brace parameters, raises ResourceError for a duplicate name, escapes literal parts with re.escape and turns each parameter into a named group that never crosses a slash. match requires a fullmatch and percent-decodes values with unquote, keeping plus signs literal. ResourceRegistry serves exact URIs before templates, tries templates in order, and raises ResourceError when nothing matches. The fixture asserts resolution, exact-over-template priority, decoding, whole-URI matching without slash crossing or unescaped dots, parameters and the duplicate error.

constraints: A duplicate template parameter raises ResourceError
Literal template text is escaped and parameters never match a slash
Values are percent-decoded while plus stays literal
Exact resources win and unmatched URIs raise ResourceError

rationale.teaches: Compile each template into an anchored regex of escaped literals and single-segment groups, and decode values only after matching.
rationale.why: Loose template matching lets a client reach a different resource path through extra segments or regex metacharacters.

ops.docstring: FastMCP-style static resources and URI templates such as users://{id}.

ops.source:
class ResourceError(Exception):
    """Raised for malformed templates and URIs that match no resource."""

candidates.why_wrong: A URI with trailing extra segments still matches the template prefix.
A parameter swallows several path segments separated by slashes.
A literal dot in the template matches any character in the URI.
A literal plus sign in a parameter is decoded into a space.
A template repeating a parameter name fails with a raw regex error.
